description:
Claims and lease recovery fail or are skipped when the data root lies outside every checkout, so a store selected through `JIT_DATA_DIR` cannot coordinate agents across linked worktrees.

## Background

Layout detection probes the selected data root (`WorktreePaths::detect_from_with_non_git_root`, `crates/jit/src/storage/worktree_paths.rs:60-104`). When that probe finds no git repository, the layout records `git_repository: false` and takes `common_dir` and `shared_jit` from `<worktree root>/.git`. It keeps only the worktree root of the checkout it finds through `relocated_worktree_checkout` and discards that checkout's common directory.

Observed with jit 1.0.0, a data root outside any repository, and `JIT_DATA_DIR` set to it:

- In the primary checkout, acquiring a lease succeeds and writes to `<primary>/.git/jit`.
- In a linked worktree, `.git` is a file. Listing and acquiring leases both fail with `Failed to create locks directory`, so that worktree cannot see or respect the primary's lease.
- In a linked worktree, worktree information reports `Type: main worktree` and `Common dir: <linked>/.git`.
- Recovery warns `Skipped claims and lease recovery because it requires a git repository` from inside a git checkout.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: With the data root outside every checkout, a primary checkout and a linked worktree of one repository use the same claims directory, under that repository's git common directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: In that layout, a lease acquired in one checkout is listed from the other, and a conflicting acquire from the other is refused as a lease conflict.
- [hard] REQ-03: In that layout, recovery run from a git checkout performs claims and lease recovery and reports no skip.
- [hard] REQ-04: In that layout, worktree information from a linked worktree reports a linked worktree and the repository's actual common directory.
- [hard] REQ-05: Run outside every git checkout, recovery still reports the skip and lease commands still fail with an error stating the cause.
- [hard] REQ-06: Layouts with the data root inside a checkout keep their current claims location.
- [hard] REQ-07: An integration test exercises REQ-01 through REQ-04 with a real linked worktree and an external data root.

## Notes

- Found while assessing a move of gf2's tracker data out of its repository. gf2 runs its agents in linked worktrees.
- This covers a data root in no repository. A data root inside its own tracker repository with a configured worktree root is specified by @/issue/5046408a.
title: Claims and lease recovery work from linked worktrees with an external data root
